summary: Umatilla NF lookout near Troy: 1925 crow's nest and 1933 CCC steel tower; unstaffed since the late 1960s or early 1970s, NRHP-listed 2015, abandoned at a 2023 visit.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab built by the CCC in 1933, beside a 1925 crow's nest in a ponderosa pine
facts.status_note: not regularly used for many years; a June 2023 visit labeled it abandoned, with the lower stairs removed

staffing.status: not staffed; ceased in the late 1960s or early 1970s

access.note: Umatilla National Forest land reached by Road 62; gated Road 090 has to be walked about 0.6 miles to the 091 spur

visit.trail_note: park on Road 62 without blocking the gate, walk 0.6 miles up Road 090, then turn right on the 091 spur (2023 visit directions)

events.note: crow's nest built by the Umatilla National Forest up a 110-foot ponderosa pine; the register gives the tree as 65 feet
CCC built the steel Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab, a cabin, garage and outhouse; the register also says around 1933
Doug Flaiz listed as known lookout personnel
approximate: the lookout ceased to be staffed in the late 1960s or early 1970s

Passport in Time volunteers worked on the cabin in September 2001; the 2023 visit calls it a restoration meant for a rental program that never happened; the nomination says the volunteers cleaned it and covered the openings
Passport in Time volunteers cleaned the garage and painted its exterior white with green trim
National Historic Lookout Register registration date September 4, 2011
added to the National Register of Historic Places as a historic district on May 26, 2015
per a 2023 visit report, the Grizzly Bear Complex fire burned through the area in 2015; the report's fire-break explanation is the writer's own guess
June 18, 2023 visit: status recorded as abandoned; lower stairs removed to keep people from going up

corrections.proposed: 1925 (crow's nest) and 1933 (CCC tower, cabin, garage and outhouse)
corrections.why: The register's own description says the lookout was built around 1933, and the NRHP nomination dates the crow's nest to 1925 and the CCC tower group to 1933. The 1935 'Built' field appears to be an error.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register names the Pomeroy Ranger District; the NRHP nomination and Wikipedia name the Walla Walla Ranger District. The story follows the nomination, which is the primary survey document.

The nomination measures the tower at 101 feet, while the register, firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 100 feet. The story says about 100 feet and notes the nomination figure; height_m uses 100 feet (30.5 m).

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the crow's nest tree is 65 feet in the register and 110 feet in the nomination; the register's 65-foot figure may describe a different tree, so the story reports both. Brief's 1935 build year is proposed for correction (see corrections). The 2001 cabin work is 'cleaned and covered openings' in the nomination but 'restored' in the 2023 visit report; both are reported. Staffing end year (1970) is approximate. The 2015 fire-break explanation is the blogger's guess and is not used as fact. Current condition comes from one June 2023 visit and the 2014-era nomination; no later source checked. Rental never happened per the 2023 visit. Access set to restricted: Forest Service land with a gated road and removed stairs. Tower 100 ft (height_m 30.5); nomination says 101 ft.
